title: 5 Rules for a JEE/NEET Study Timetable That Doesn't Burn You Out
description: Almost every JEE and NEET timetable dies within a few weeks. Here are the 5 rules behind a structure built to actually survive contact with real life.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: Most JEE and NEET timetables die the same way. Five subjects a day. Mock tests every Sunday. Zero gaps. Looks great on paper. Falls apart in two weeks.
It's not a willpower problem. It's a design problem. Here's a structure that actually holds up.

content.heading: Match subjects to your energy
list: Track your focus for 3 days. No plan yet, just notice.
Find your 1-2 high-energy windows.
Put your hardest subject there. Usually Physics or Organic Chem.
Use low-energy time for revision or flashcards, not fresh problems.

content.heading: Fix your subject rotation
list: Don't decide what to study each morning. That decision alone drains you.
Set a weekly pattern: Physics + Maths on Mon/Thu.
Chemistry + Biology on Tue/Fri.
One mixed revision day midweek.
The only choice left each day is: start.

content.heading: Leave real slack
list: Zero buffer means zero room for a bad day.
Leave one unscheduled block, every single day.
Keep one lighter day per week.
This is what stops a bad day from becoming a bad week.

content.heading: Give revision its own slot
list: Revision is not leftover time.
New content means nothing if it's gone by exam day.
Fix a slot: last 45 minutes daily, or one evening a week.
Non-negotiable. Not "if there's time."

content.heading: Take a full day off
list: One full day off, every week.
Not lighter. Off.
Skip it too long and you don't save time, you lose 3 days to a crash.
This is the step people cut first and regret most.

content.body: None of this is complicated. It's just permission to build a plan you can actually keep.
